body:
Adversarial review, round 1 — read-only on the diff, plus one mistake of my own made while checking it.

## Findings

**#700 — the unified snapshot still publishes the 30 names, and I did not fix it here.** `UNIFIED_INGREDIENT_MAPPING.tsv` carries `Cadmium(II) nitrate` on the `CHEBI:64205` row, and the rest. A rebuild removes all of them (claw's unified builder honours `REJECTED_LABEL`), but against current CultureMech it moves **752 rows** and drops **124 net** — 194 of them in identity columns. CultureMech was clean and on `main`, so that is real upstream movement since 2026-09-12. A refresh that size needs its own reviewed row-set diff against a pinned CultureMech rev. Hand-deleting 30 tokens from a generated file is what the #653 gate exists to refuse, so I did not do that either.

**`just rebuild-unified` was broken, fixed in `a60d678d`.** claw now raises `MechRootError` when `CULTUREMECH_ROOT` is unset even if `--culturemech` is passed. The recipe sets the environment too, and takes `OUTPUT` so the build line can be tested without touching the tracked file — proven with the recipe's own relative defaults.

## A mistake I made during this review

Rebuilding the snapshot by hand, I chained the stamp after the build **unconditionally**. The build failed, the TSV did not change, and the stamp recorded the stale, still-contaminated file as current against the new inputs — a provenance sidecar asserting something false, written by the very tool meant to prevent that. I caught it because the row-set comparison came back "0 rows changed" when I expected ten, and reverted both files before anything was committed.

The checked-in recipe was never exposed — each `just` line is its own shell, so a failed build aborts before the stamp — but the ordering is now explained in a comment, because it is load-bearing and did not look it.

## Checked and clean

- **The backfill cannot put them back.** `backfill_sssom_surface_forms` builds its "existing" set from every synonym entry regardless of type, so a `REJECTED_LABEL` counts as present and is not re-added.
- **No field loss on the ten records** across three `sync-curated` runs — compared key by key against `HEAD`; only `synonyms` and `curation_history` moved.
- **All ten `other` cells match claw's merged builder**, and the rebuild now shows 0 subject churn in either direction (it showed 8 before #698's fix).
- **`mapped_count`** moved 2618 → 2616 because it was already stale on `main`; no record's status changed here.

## Deliberately left for a curator

Still baselined: 40 kg-microbe round-trip pairs, and 19 in MIM's own YAML that are *related* forms rather than unrelated compounds — `L-Asparagine`/`ASPARAGINE` and six more stereo-vs-generic pairs, `Vitamin B12`↔`Cyanocobalamin` each claiming the other's name, `L-Cysteine`/its zwitterion, and two hydrate pairs sharing one identifier (#459's cohort). Each needs a ruling about the record, not a mechanical rule.

Adversarial review, round 2 — this time **not by me**. Twenty-five independent reviewers: two skeptics per retirement told to *refute* it (one from nomenclature, one from the ChEBI graph), and three over the code.

## The retirements hold

22 verdicts, **0 refuted, all high confidence.** Each skeptic re-derived formulas, InChIKeys and edges from `chebi.db` and looked for any 1–2 hop path between the record's term and the "wrong" one. None found one.

## The code did not — four real defects, all mine

**#701 — my tombstone fix over-corrected, and would have shipped a regression.** Making a `REJECTED` record stop owning its name was right; I implemented it as `continue`, which left the name with *no owner*. Rule K then let **any** record publish ~60 tombstone names. The reviewer ran `main`'s validator beside the branch's:

```
evaluate_rule_k([{'subject_id': 'MIM:Feso4', 'other': 'FeSO4 x 7H2O'}])   main: flagged   branch: []
```

The test I wrote pinned the bug — it asserted the name was *absent* from the owner map. Now the name is **credited to the live record sharing the tombstone's identifier** (all 63 tombstones have one; 59 have exactly one), and a REJECTED record with no such sibling keeps its own name, since "REJECTED means merged" is an observation about the corpus, not an invariant. Re-measured: the three probes are flagged again, the true target still passes, and live violations equal the baseline exactly (59 / 0 unbaselined / 0 unused) — so all 51 pairs I dropped *were* legitimate.

**A miscount.** "21 records lost continuity" counted the 11 backup *files* as records. It is **10 records**, 8 renamed, all 8 published subjects. Counting backups as records is the defect this branch fixes. Corrected here and on #698.

**An untested half.** Reverting the freshness digest to `rglob` left the suite green. It has a regression test now, mutation-checked.

**claw's unified builder reads the backups too** — 2,962 "records" from a tree of 2,951, and because its index is first-writer-wins over sorted paths, a **stale backup beats the live record** for any stem sorting after `backups`. Fixed at the source in claw#458 rather than followed by MIM's digest.

## What the skeptics noticed in passing turned out to matter most

One saw that 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid's CAS `156-38-7` is `CHEBI:156387` de-hyphenated. It is a pattern — **#702**: eleven records were once mapped to `CHEBI:<their own CAS>`. All were corrected; three still carried the residue, **5 more synonyms, all live in published `other`** (a fluorescent dye's name on L-cysteine HCl, `Fuc(a1-3)[Glc(a1-4)]Gal` on disodium succinate). Retired in `4ba911c5`: **35 synonyms on 13 records** in total.

Also filed: **#703** (46 trait phrases such as `produces: actinomycin A` published as compound synonyms) and **#704** (three curator calls).

## And one correction to my own gating

My earlier "CI green" was wrong: `pytest` had **failed** on two repo guards my new script tripped. My poll counted rows reading `fail`/`pending` and found none at a moment when the old runs were cancelled and the new ones not yet listed — a denylist reads those as green. I now gate on an allowlist: every check-run on the head SHA must be `completed/success`.
